plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) if I win, bidding exactly my value of $6 ensures I only win when profitable (value ≥ price paid) and never overpay. Bidding higher risks winning at a loss; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, the optimal bid is my true value: $6.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others bid. If I bid exactly my value ($40), I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and I pay that second-highest price - guaranteeing non-negative profit. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if others bid high; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With no prior history to adjust for, truthful bidding is optimal.

This is a second-price auction with independent private values uniformly distributed on [0,49]. In a second-price auction, the dominant strategy is to bid one's true value, regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. Bidding exactly my value ensures that if I win, I pay less than my value (profit ≥ 0), and if I lose, it's because someone valued it more than me. There's no incentive to bid higher or lower than true value. Therefore, I will bid $28.
